_doc: The Codex: who's who in this Gotham — vital details for the family, the people round them and the rogues. Heights and weights follow DC's own listings where there are any; dates DC never fixed are this world's, kept consistent. Only `contact` entries are in his phone; everyone else is reached through someone who knows them (`reach`).

people.name: Bruce Wayne
people.bio: Orphaned in Crime Alley at eight, trained across the world for twelve years, and came home to make the city's criminals afraid of the dark. The family he swore he wouldn't have found him anyway.

people.name: Alfred Pennyworth
people.occupation: Butler; field medic; the household's conscience
people.bio: Ex-SAS, ex-actor, and the man who raised Bruce after the alley. Runs the Manor, the cave's medbay and everyone's guilt with the same dry efficiency.

people.name: Dick Grayson
people.bio: The Flying Graysons' son and the first Robin. Took his own name and his own city; still the one everyone in the family actually calls. Haley, his three-legged dog, runs the apartment.

people.name: Jason Todd
people.bio: The street kid who stole the Batmobile's tyres and became the second Robin; killed by the Joker, brought back by a Lazarus Pit. Kills the worst, protects the kids, and comes when it counts.

people.name: Randy Wayne
people.bio: Bruce and Selina's son, raised at the Manor and made Robin between Jason and Tim. Walked out angry, flies Lucius's Batwing suit alone, and answers Dick and Cass more than his father.

people.name: Tim Drake
people.occupation: Robin; Drake Industries heir; perpetually postponed student
people.bio: Worked out who Batman and Robin were at nine and talked his way into the role. The family's best pure detective after Bruce — maybe. Runs on coffee; dating Bernard.

people.name: Barbara Gordon
people.occupation: Batgirl; Oracle — the family's intelligence network
people.bio: Jim Gordon's daughter, a peer rather than a protégé. Runs the network everyone depends on and tells Bruce he's wrong on an open channel.

people.name: Cassandra Cain
people.bio: Raised by David Cain to read bodies instead of words, she learned to speak late and fights better than anyone alive. Says little, sees everything, and calls Bruce 'Dad' only when it matters most.

people.name: Lucius Fox
people.bio: Keeps the company honest and the family's gear working, and knows exactly what the R&D line marked 'miscellaneous' is. Married to Tanya; father of Luke.

people.name: Selina Kyle
people.occupation: Thief, by choice and by trade
people.bio: The East End's master thief and Bruce's equal and opposite. Gave their son to Bruce to raise and has never made her peace with it. Knows who he is; doesn't know about the kids.

people.name: James Gordon
people.bio: The one honest cop who stayed, and Barbara's father. Lights the signal; asks no questions he doesn't want answered.

people.name: Dr. Leslie Thompkins
people.occupation: Physician; runs the free clinic on Park Row
people.bio: Held Bruce the night his parents died. Patches up anyone who walks into her clinic, masks included, and lectures all of them.

people.name: Harvey Bullock
people.bio: Slob, cynic, and a better detective than he lets anyone see. Hates the masks on principle; takes their tips anyway.

people.name: Renee Montoya
people.bio: Tough, straight, and done pretending the department's clean. One of the few cops the family trusts.

people.name: Stephanie Brown
people.bio: Cass's best friend and the loudest person in any room. Was Robin for about five minutes and will tell you about it.

people.name: Bernard Dowd
people.bio: Tim's boyfriend. Wants Tim to sleep more, and is winning, slowly.

people.name: Haley
people.bio: Dick's three-legged dog, rescued from a tracksuit gang. Has opinions about pasta and none about patrol.

people.name: Tanya Fox
people.bio: Tells Lucius he uses the thumbs-up wrong. Is right.

people.name: Luke Fox
people.bio: Lucius's son, an engineer himself — and, in this world, not the one in the Batwing suit.

people.name: Vicki Vale
people.bio: Gotham's best investigative reporter and the one who's come closest to working out who Bruce Wayne is at night. Dated him once; still suspects him always.

people.name: Talia al Ghul
people.bio: Ra's al Ghul's daughter, Bruce's oldest and most dangerous love. She pulled Jason out of a Lazarus Pit; nobody reaches her unless she wants to be reached.

people.name: Kate Kane
people.bio: Bruce's cousin on his mother's side, thrown out of West Point and into the night. Works her own side of Gotham, her own way, and keeps the family at a careful arm's length.

people.name: Duke Thomas
people.bio: A Narrows kid who refused to look away. Sees light the rest of them can't and works the hours they sleep through: Gotham by day.

people.name: Clark Kent
people.bio: A Kansas farm boy in Metropolis, and Bruce's closest friend outside the cave — whatever either of them would say about it.

people.name: Christopher Nakano
people.home: The mayor's residence, Upper East Side
people.bio: A law-and-order mayor who ran on cleaning up the city and means the vigilantes too: he's spent his term trying to make the masks illegal and the drones legal. Up for re-election in November against Marion Grange, and not as safe as he'd like.

people.name: Marion Grange
people.bio: Councilwoman for the Narrows and Coventry, running against Nakano on housing, police reform and the Narrows rebuilding money. Says what she thinks of the vigilantes depends on what they're stopping.

people.name: Janet Van Dorn
people.bio: Tough, ambitious and very good at her job; puts away what the GCPD brings her and makes speeches about the rest. Nakano's DA, for now.

people.name: Evelyn Adams
people.bio: The Gazette's crime desk: first at every scene, a scanner on her nightstand and no friends at City Hall. Writes the morning's worst before the coffee's on; owes nobody.

people.name: Jack Ryder
people.bio: GBS's nightly loudmouth — ratings over truth, every time. Hates the vigilantes on Mondays and loves them on Fridays, depending on what played.

people.name: Summer Gleeson
people.bio: GCN's six o'clock anchor — weather, traffic and the human story; the face half of Gotham has dinner with.

people.name: Alexander Knox
people.bio: Follows the money and sees bats in every shadow; on the Narrows audit and Daggett's contracts this month, and closer than Daggett would like.

people.name: Simon Saint
people.bio: Drones, security contracts and the mayor's ear. Wants Gotham policed by machines he builds, and has the donations on record to prove he means it.

people.name: Roland Daggett
people.bio: Developer behind half the Narrows rebuilding contracts — and the audit into them. Smiles in photographs with whoever is mayor.

The Joker.bio: Nobody knows his name, his face before the chemicals, or what he wants beyond the joke. He's killed hundreds, crippled Barbara, murdered Jason, and he will be back — Arkham is a hotel to him.
The Joker.associates: Harley Quinn; hired crews that rarely survive the job
The Joker.weakness: Needs an audience — and Batman, specifically
The Joker.contingency: Never alone with him. Antidote to his toxins stocked in every vehicle; Arkham's wing holds him only as long as he lets it.

Harley Quinn.bio: Dr. Harleen Quinzel fell for the patient she was treating and followed him over the edge. Out from under him now, mostly — a chaos agent with a mallet and a loyal crew, and a heart she'd deny having.
Harley Quinn.associates: Poison Ivy; her own crew; the Joker, on and off
Harley Quinn.contingency: Separate her from the Joker and she can be talked down. Ivy's the lever.

The Penguin.bio: Oswald Cobblepot runs the Iceberg Lounge and, behind its bar, half of Gotham's smuggling. Old money that went bad; never holds the gun, always holds the ledger.
The Penguin.associates: The Iceberg Lounge staff; harbour crews; councillors on retainer
The Penguin.weakness: Vanity, and the respectability he can't buy
The Penguin.contingency: Follow the money, not the man — his books put him away; his fists never will.

The Riddler.bio: Edward Nygma has to prove he's the smartest man in the room, so he leaves a riddle with every crime. Deathtraps, ciphers, and an ego that is his own worst enemy.
The Riddler.contingency: Solve it faster than he expects, then don't tell him how — the not-knowing breaks him.

Two-Face.bio: Harvey Dent was Gotham's best district attorney until Maroni's acid split his face and his mind. Every choice now goes to the coin; every crime comes in twos.
Two-Face.associates: Twin-themed crews; the Falcones, on and off
Two-Face.weakness: The coin — and the Harvey still in there
Two-Face.contingency: Talk to Harvey, not Two-Face. Control the coin and you control the outcome.

Scarecrow.bio: Dr. Jonathan Crane, a psychologist who weaponised fear itself. His toxin makes you live your worst terror; he studies what's left of you afterwards.
Scarecrow.associates: Hired thugs; occasionally the League of Shadows
Scarecrow.weakness: His own fear — of bats, of being afraid
Scarecrow.contingency: Filters in every cowl; antidote in every belt. Don't fight in the dark he's chosen.

Poison Ivy.bio: Dr. Pamela Isley, botanist turned plant elemental. She'd raze Gotham to let the trees back in, and her pheromones make men want to help her do it.
Poison Ivy.contingency: Women and filtered air against the pheromones. Never fight her in a greenhouse.

Mr. Freeze.bio: Dr. Victor Fries steals for the research that might cure his wife, Nora, frozen for years in her chamber. The suit keeps him alive at sub-zero; the cause makes him merciless.
Mr. Freeze.contingency: Thermite and a heat source; threaten the suit, never Nora.

Bane.bio: Raised in a prison called Peña Duro, educated in its library, built by Venom. The only man who broke Batman's back — a strategist first, a giant second.
Bane.contingency: Cut the Venom lines. Never let him choose the ground or the timing.

Killer Croc.bio: Waylon Jones, born with a skin condition that turned him into something else, lives under the docks and eats what he catches. Not all of it is fish.
Killer Croc.weakness: Cold, and smell — he tracks by scent
Killer Croc.contingency: Stay out of the water and the sewers. Sedatives sized for an elephant.

Black Mask.bio: Roman Sionis, cosmetics heir and False Face Society boss, wears a mask carved from his father's coffin. Torture is how he manages people.
Black Mask.weakness: Rage — he can't stand being disrespected
Black Mask.contingency: Turn his lieutenants. He kills the ones he suspects, so make him suspect them.

Mad Hatter.bio: Jervis Tetch builds mind-control tech into hats and lives out Alice in Wonderland with real people. The young women he 'casts' as Alice are why he's never getting out.
Mad Hatter.contingency: Shielded cowls against his frequencies. Find the hat, find the signal.

Victor Zsasz.bio: A serial killer who believes he's freeing his victims, and carves a tally mark into his own skin for every one. No ideology, no endgame — just the count.
Victor Zsasz.contingency: Never let him reach a crowd. Arkham's maximum wing, permanently.

Firefly.bio: Garfield Lynns, a pyrotechnics expert turned arsonist in a jetpack and flame-retardant suit. He sets fires to watch them burn, and Gotham has a lot of old wood.
Firefly.contingency: Fire crews on standby. Ground him — shoot the jetpack, not the man.

Hush.bio: Dr. Thomas Elliot grew up with Bruce and hated him for everything he had. A brilliant surgeon in bandages who knows who Batman is — and plays the long game.
Hush.contingency: He knows the secret. Everything he holds must be assumed compromised; keep the family's identities moving.

Clayface.bio: Basil Karlo, a failed actor whose body became living clay. He can be anyone — which means the person you're talking to might not be them.
Clayface.contingency: Challenge phrases with the family. Sonic and electrical disruptors.

The Ventriloquist.bio: Arnold Wesker is meek and harmless; Scarface, the dummy on his arm, runs a gang and orders hits. Separate them and Wesker begs for his life.

Professor Pyg.bio: Lazlo Valentin, surgeon in a pig mask, 'perfects' his victims into mindless Dollotrons. The surgery doesn't come out.
Professor Pyg.contingency: Find the operating theatre fast — every hour is another victim.

Calendar Man.bio: Julian Day commits crimes on holidays and anniversaries, and talks in dates. From his cell he's a consultant the GCPD hates using.
Calendar Man.contingency: Watch the holidays. Use him, never trust him.

Deathstroke.bio: Slade Wilson, enhanced super-soldier and the world's most expensive mercenary. In Gotham only when someone's paid for a death.
Deathstroke.contingency: Find who hired him and void the contract. Never fight him fair.

Ra's al Ghul.bio: The Demon's Head, centuries old through the Lazarus Pits, commands the League of Assassins and wants to cleanse the world. He considers Bruce his heir.
Ra's al Ghul.weakness: The Pits — and his respect for Bruce
Ra's al Ghul.contingency: Find the nearest Lazarus Pit. Talia is the only door that opens.

Hugo Strange.bio: A psychiatrist who's studied Batman for years and believes he knows him better than he knows himself. Wants to become him, or own him.
Hugo Strange.contingency: Assume he's profiled the whole family. Change patterns he'd predict.

Man-Bat.bio: Dr. Kirk Langstrom tried to cure his deafness with bat DNA and became something else. More tragedy than villain — when he's himself.
Man-Bat.associates: His wife, Francine, who keeps the cure
Man-Bat.contingency: Sonic emitter, then the serum. He's a patient, not a target.

Carmine Falcone.bio: The Roman: Gotham's old-money mob boss, with judges and police on his payroll since before Bruce wore the cowl.
Carmine Falcone.contingency: Gordon and the books. RICO, not fists.

Sal Maroni.bio: Falcone's rival, the man who threw acid in Harvey Dent's face. Locked up, still running rackets through his lawyers.
Sal Maroni.contingency: Keep him away from Harvey — for Harvey's sake as much as his.

Rupert Thorne.bio: A crime boss who owns councilmen and keeps his own hands clean. Debts always collected; never by him.
Rupert Thorne.contingency: Follow the council votes. His money talks, so listen.

Killer Moth.bio: Drury Walker, a costumed thief with a moth suit and a grudge — more nuisance than menace, and furious that nobody takes him seriously.
Killer Moth.contingency: Tim can handle it. Tim insists on handling it.

The Court of Owls.bio: A secret society of Gotham's oldest families, older than its charter, with undying Talons that kill for it. Most say it's a nursery rhyme. Bruce knows it isn't.
The Court of Owls.associates: The Talons; old families nobody suspects
The Court of Owls.contingency: Cold storage for any Talon. Trust no one whose family name is on a Gotham street sign.
